# The national-statistics pack

*National statistics* · version 1.0.0 · code `STCAN`

## What it is

Statistics Canada's headline statistics by vector from its Web Data Service (Statistics Canada Open Licence): the consumer price index, unemployment, monthly GDP, population, housing starts and the overnight money market rate. Each series shows its latest value, the change on the period and on the year, and its history. Filled daily by the national-statistics feed into the worldlake lake; more vectors are a line each in the feed's YAML.

## Data structures

Every kind the pack owns, read from its manifest, its samples and its Sutras: how its ids look, its fields (type, an example, what it means), its nested lists and the fields that link to other kinds. A path `A[].B` is field `B` of every element of list `A`.

### `statistics-series`

**National statistic** · mnemonic `NSTAT` · read through connector `statistics-store`.

**Id:** field `SERIES_ID`; pattern `^NSTAT-`; for example `NSTAT-V1`.

Fields, from 7 sample documents:

| Field | Type | Example | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CHANGE` | number | `80343.0` | The latest value less the previous one. |
| `CHANGE_PCT` | number | `0.1926` | The change on the period in per cent. (%) |
| `FREQUENCY` | string | `quarterly` | How often the series is published (Statistics Canada's frequency code, or the feed's YAML when it says). |
| `GEOGRAPHY` | string | `Canada` | The series' first member: its geography. |
| `HISTORY` | list of objects |  | The value by reference period, oldest first, over the feed's history-periods (PERIOD, VALUE). |
| `LATEST` | number | `41798407.0` | The latest published value, in the unit and scale shown. |
| `LATEST_PERIOD` | date | `2026-07-01` | The reference period of the latest value (its first day). |
| `MEMBERS` | null |  | The table's dimension members that make the series, as Statistics Canada names them (Canada;All-items). |
| `NAME` | string | `Population of Canada` | The series' title in the feed's YAML, as NAME for search. |
| `PREVIOUS` | number | `41718064.0` | The value of the period before. |
| `PREVIOUS_PERIOD` | date | `2026-04-01` | The reference period of the previous value. |
| `PROVENANCE` | object |  | Where the record comes from, one object: SOURCE, DATASET, RETRIEVED_AT, LICENCE, ATTRIBUTION, URL and INTERNAL_ONLY. |
| `RELEASED` | timestamp | `2026-09-23T08:30` | When Statistics Canada released the latest value (Eastern time). |
| `SCALE` | string | `units` | The scalar factor the values carry (units, thousands, millions). |
| `SERIES_ID` | string | `NSTAT-V1` | NSTAT-V and the Statistics Canada vector number. |
| `TABLE_ID` | string | `17-10-0009-01` | The Statistics Canada table number (18-10-0004-01). |
| `TABLE_TITLE` | string | `Population estimates, quarterly` | The table's title in the feed's YAML. |
| `TITLE` | string | `Population of Canada` | The series' title in the feed's YAML. |
| `TOPIC` | string | `Population` | The theme the feed's YAML gives the series (Prices, Labour, Output, Population, Housing, Money markets). |
| `UNIT` | string | `persons` | What the value measures, from the feed's YAML (an index, %, CAD, persons, units). |
| `VECTOR` | string | `v1` | The Statistics Canada vector id (v and a number): one series of one table. |
| `YEAR_ON_YEAR_PCT` | number | `0.4553` | The change on the same period a year before, in per cent; empty when the history is shorter. (%) |

Nested structures:

| Path | Fields |
|---|---|
| `HISTORY[]` | `PERIOD` (date): The reference period (its first day)., `VALUE` (number): The published value for that period. |
| `PROVENANCE` | `ATTRIBUTION` (string): The credit line to repeat when the data is shown or republished., `DATASET` (string): The Statistics Canada table and vector the record was built from., `INTERNAL_ONLY` (boolean): True when the source's terms forbid redistribution outside the organisation (Export data refuses the record)., `LICENCE` (string): The terms under which the source allows reuse, as recorded in the feed's YAML., `RETRIEVED_AT` (date): The business date of the feed's pull that wrote the record., `SOURCE` (string): The organisation whose published data the record holds., `URL` (string): The table's page on the Statistics Canada website. |

## Refreshing the data

The **national-statistics** feed (`config/feeds/national-statistics.yaml`: its sources and their licences in `options.sources`, its schedule, weekdays at 09:00 local time, and its selection in `options`) pulls what is new into `<data>/datafeeds/national-statistics/<date>/` and loads it into the `worldlake` lake: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics` (the parallel loader), `--load inbox` (the server's data inbox loads it), `--dry-run` (what it would ask). With the Python you run Drishti with: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics` on Linux and macOS, `py -3.13 tools\drishti.py feed run national-statistics` on Windows; the schedule for cron, systemd or Task Scheduler: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed schedule`. It needs no key. The pack's data is its committed snapshot, `data/testdata/national-statistics/<kind>/`, from a live run: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics --snapshot` pulls the latest data and rewrites it, with the pack's reference samples (a few documents of each kind for this README and the docs, never served) and this README; `python3 tools/drishti.py lake demo` builds the snapshot into the lake the connector reads.

The data feed `national-statistics` (config/feeds/national-statistics.yaml) pulls `statistics-series`: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics` fetches them daily into `data/datafeeds/national-statistics/<date>/` and loads them into the lake `worldlake`; `--dry-run` says what it would fetch, changing nothing; `--snapshot` refreshes the committed snapshot in data/testdata instead; `feed status` shows the last runs. The External data feeds guide (docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md) has the schedule entries for Linux and Windows.

The pack's files are written by `tools/packgen/publicsector/make.py`; its `--check` fails when the committed files differ from what it would write.

## Data contracts

Every kind of the pack has a data contract: a YAML file beside the pack (`modules/external-data/packs/national-statistics/contracts/<kind>.contract.yaml`, checked against `tools/contracts.schema.json`) that says what one record is, its key, how it is stored and dated, and every field with its type, presence, unit and meaning. The contracts are published on [docs/contracts/packs/national-statistics.md](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/national-statistics.md) and each kind's example (a real record of the test data, every field explained) on [docs/contracts/packs](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/README.md); this README links them and copies neither. Check them against the pack and its data with `python3 tools/contracts.py check` (or `drishti.py contract check`); show one with `python3 tools/contracts.py show <MNEMONIC>`.

| Command | Kind | Class | Key | Grain | Contract | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NSTAT` | `statistics-series` | fundamental | `SERIES_ID` | One row per national statistic, keyed by SERIES_ID. | [NSTAT: National statistic](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/national-statistics.md#nstat-national-statistic-statistics-series) (`contracts/statistics-series.contract.yaml`) | [example](../../../../docs/contracts/packs/national-statistics.md#example-national-statistics-statistics-series) |

*Class*: **fundamental** data is delivered by a source system and stored; **input** is stored data an engine reads; **computed** is worked out by Drishti when asked and never stored by a source; **drishti-owned** is kept by Drishti itself.

## Data retrieval

Where each kind's data comes from, how it reaches the lake and how to check it. Three origins: **external** data, fetched from a public source by its data feed (each source, its licence and worked examples on the [External data](../../../../docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md) help page); **synthetic** test data (or hand-written reference data), written by a generator with fictitious names; **computed** by a Drishti engine when it is asked, never stored by a source.

| Command | Kind | Origin | How it reaches Drishti |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NSTAT` | `statistics-series` | external: Statistics Canada Web Data Service (Statistics Canada Open Licence) — refreshed by `drishti.py feed run national-statistics` | the daily feed `national-statistics` → `<data>/delta/worldlake/statistics/statistics-series/` (lake `worldlake`) → connector `statistics-store`; the committed snapshot `data/testdata/national-statistics/statistics-series/` (7 documents, retrieved 2026-11-27) → `lake demo` → the lake `worldlake`, same connector |

### External sources

| Source | Where | Licence | Internal only | Refresh |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Statistics Canada Web Data Service | https://www150.statcan.gc.ca/t1/wds/rest | Statistics Canada Open Licence | no | `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics` |

Run these from the Drishti folder (the repository root, or the install folder of a release).

```bash
python3 tools/drishti.py feed status national-statistics            # its last runs: last success, rows, failures (offline: the run ledger)
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics --dry-run     # what would be fetched and loaded; changes nothing
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics               # pull today's data and load it into the lake `worldlake` (what the daily schedule runs)
python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics --load inbox  # the same through the data inbox: the server loads it
```

The same with the Python you run Drishti with: `python3 tools/drishti.py feed run national-statistics` on Linux and macOS, `py tools\drishti.py feed run national-statistics` on Windows (every argument is passed on); the daily schedule entries: `drishti.py feed schedule --cron` (or `--systemd`, `--windows`) ([WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md](../../../../docs/guides/WORLD_DATA_GUIDE.md)).

### Into the lake, checking, offline

- **The lake.** `python3 tools/drishti.py lake demo` reads `data/testdata/testdata.yaml` and writes every dataset (test data, the committed public-data snapshots) into `<data>/delta/<domain>/<kind>/`, where the pack's Delta connector serves it; a computed kind needs nothing loaded. `lake build` loads your own large JSON exports the same way ([Command line](../../../../docs/guides/CLI_REFERENCE.md)).
- **Checking.** `python3 tools/contracts.py check` compares every contract with the pack and its data; each generator's `--check` (above) fails when the committed files differ from what it would write; in the console, `<MNEMONIC> <GO>` lists a kind and the pack's code opens its overview with the count of each kind.
- **Offline.** Everything committed works without a network: the test data and the public-data snapshots are in the repository and `lake demo` reads only them. A data feed runs offline from its download cache (`--offline`); a connector that reaches the internet (news, yfinance, the public-data feeds) is off as shipped and never starts on a machine configured offline (`drishti.offline.plugins`).
